note: The board: ten tracked theatres with a dated log of facts per theatre. The morning run appends one entry per theatre that had a reportable event (newest last) with the cited source rows copied into src, and never edits or deletes old entries. No status labels: the page derives activity from the dates. lat/lon place the marker on the schematic map. short = map label; lp = label position (above, below, left, right).

log.t: The six-day Oleshky (Kherson) ceasefire expired 20:59 GMT on 1 Nov; Russia reportedly refused an extension. The Kremlin says three-way talks in Abu Dhabi come after 4 Nov. The State Department approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 interceptors to Ukraine on 30 Oct. [25, 27, 28]
src: Kherson braces as localised truce ends
Kremlin: Abu Dhabi talks after November 4

log.t: Russia launched 289 drones and 59 cruise missiles overnight; President Zelensky put the ballistic total at 17, and the Energy Ministry says energy sites in 10 regions were hit. [13, 14, 15] Envoy Steve Witkoff says the US will mediate working-level Ukraine–Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov. The toll from the bombing of an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 29, with 48 missing. [18, 17]
src: Air defense downs 49 of 59 cruise missiles, 257 of 289 drones overnight; strikes recorded at 23 locations
On U.S. Election Day, Russia launched 17 ballistic missiles and 289 drones at Ukraine, according to Zelenskyy
Russian attack hits energy infrastructure in 10 regions, Energy Ministry says
Ukraine and Russia will hold talks in Abu Dhabi with US mediation
Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing

log.t: Witkoff confirmed US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov, with Medinsky leading Russia's delegation; Russian drones hit a substation serving the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant. [12, 14]
src: Witkoff reveals location, date for new trilateral peace deal negotiations
Russia targets substation critical to stable operation of Khmelnytskyi NPP

log.t: The European Commission hosted post-war prosperity talks with Ukraine, the US, Germany, France, Britain, NATO and the World Bank on 4 Nov; Zelensky put the 2 Nov Komyshuvakha toll at 40. [12, 15]
src: Statement following meeting on prosperity talks today (STATEMENT/26/2348)
Zelensky: Death toll in Komyshuvakha rises to 40, more than 30 may remain trapped under rubble

log.t: Melania Trump hosted Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and Ukrainian officials Davyd Arakhamia and Dmytro Lubinets at the White House on 5 Nov; President Trump met Dmitriev separately. Russia launched 128 drones and two Kh-35 missiles overnight into 5 Nov and the Air Force reported 105 drones downed; the Komyshuvakha toll reached 43. [12, 15, 16]
src: First lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials. Trump met with Putin's envoy
Shot down or suppressed: 105 enemy targets (statement for the night of 4–5 Nov)
Death toll from Russian airstrike on Komyshuvakha rises to 43 – Zelensky

log.t: President Putin said on 6 Nov that trilateral talks will be held in the United Arab Emirates on Tue 10 Nov; Arakhamia said Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's delegation. Russia launched 227 drones overnight into 6 Nov and the Air Force reported 196 downed; missiles hit Kyiv overnight into 7 Nov, wounding at least three. [9, 10, 124, 12]
src: Putin discusses November 10 talks in Abu Dhabi with Security Council
Umerov to lead Ukraine delegation in Abu Dhabi peace talks despite media confusion, top official confirms
ADF neutralizes 196 Russian drones used to attack Ukraine overnight
Russian ballistic missiles slam Kyiv, injuring 3, including child, after Zelensky warns of mass attack

log.t: Russia launched 172 drones and Iskander-M, Zircon, KN-23 and S-400 missiles overnight into 7 Nov, mainly at Kyiv region; the Air Force reported 4 missiles and 149 drones downed and President Zelensky gave 36 ballistic missiles. Substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants were hit and six people were injured in Kyiv. Ukraine's General Staff said Neptune missiles hit the Proton-Electrotex plant in Oryol. Medinsky leads Russia's delegation to Abu Dhabi for 10–11 Nov. [10, 11, 12, 20, 170, 19]
src: Air defense downs four missiles, 149 drones used by Russia to attack Ukraine overnight
Russia may have used North Korean KN-23 missiles to strike Ukrainian energy facility: Zelensky
Zelensky: In addition to Kyiv, 12 regions of Ukraine come under attack overnight
Injury toll after Russian attack on Kyiv rises to six, including one child
Ukrainian forces strike Proton plant in Oryol with Neptune missiles: General Staff
Russia to send senior diplomats, military officials to upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi

log.t: The IRGC navy says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 31 Oct. Qatari-mediated talks broke up 1–2 Nov with a draft still circulating. [28]

A US official called Monday's strike on Qeshm Island a defensive measure against Iranian surface-to-air missiles; IRNA reported that the Revolutionary Guards destroyed a US MQ-9 drone east of the strait. [9, 10] Araghchi says Hormuz reopens on day two if Washington meets Iran's conditions first; Qatari mediators took a draft text to Tehran on 2 Nov. Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday. [11, 9, 101]
src: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Vance seeks settlement
US hits Qeshm Island, Pezeshkian signals more diplomacy: Iran war latest
Araghchi says Hormuz could be reopened within two days if conditions met
Crude oil prices sell off more than 7% on Iran peace talk hopes ahead of U.S. midterms

log.t: Qatari mediators await US and Iranian answers to a draft within 36 hours; India says an Indian seafarer was killed in an attack on a dhow near Limah, Oman. [19, 20]
src: Iran, US still far apart on deal to end war as Qatar pushes mediation
Iran and the United States strike Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz

log.t: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said US power is in “irreversible decline”; the IRGC claims four tankers struck mines south of the strait and a US MQ-9 was downed, without comment from CENTCOM; Brent settled at $94.62 on 4 Nov, down 8.7%. [18, 19, 86]
src: Iran claims strikes on multiple tankers, emboldened after US elections
Crude oil prices fall below $90 a barrel as Vance blames GOP election defeat on Iran war

log.t: A senior Iranian official said Iran sent the US a nuclear proposal through Qatar, to be discussed only after seven demands are met; President Trump said of a decision on the war: “You'll know soon enough.” The Revolutionary Guards said three tankers were damaged on 5 Nov; Brent settled at $98.29. [17, 18, 19, 91]
src: Iran sent nuclear proposal to the US via Qatar, senior Iranian official says
Trump meets with national security team, says Iran war decision coming "soon"
Iran reports three tankers damaged in Hormuz on November 5
Daily closes: S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq Composite, Russell 2000, AEX, Stoxx 600, DAX, Brent, WTI, TTF, gold, VIX

log.t: Iranian state media reported two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island on 6 Nov after a US strike on an air-defence system; President Trump: “We do minor strikes.” The IRGC said two tankers hit mines; UKMTO reported an explosion on a tanker leaving the strait, crew safe. [14, 15]
src: US military carries out new targeted strike on Iran as Tehran's leaders weigh mediators' proposals

log.t: The IRGC navy said two tankers hit mines and burned on 7 Nov, one inside the strait; Iranian agencies reported explosions on Qeshm and at Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas. CENTCOM formed Task Force Iron Gate for Iran's land borders and the Caspian, and a US aircraft fired on the M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi said Iran's missile-range limit has been lifted. [24, 25, 15, 26]
src: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 2 oil tankers hit mines, caught fire near Strait of Hormuz
Explosions heard in southern Iran's Qeshm, Jask: report
Iran's IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage

log.t: Gaza civil defence said Israeli attacks killed five people on 2 Nov in Khan Younis, Gaza City and central Gaza; health officials count at least 1,580 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel's military said it killed six Hamas members for ceasefire violations. [131, 132]
src: Israeli attacks kill five in Gaza Strip

log.t: Gaza's health ministry counts 1,593 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire after five deaths on 2 Nov; Israel asked Lebanon, through the US, to deploy its army and set up checkpoints in Hezbollah areas. [127]
src: Israeli forces kill four in Gaza as fifth Palestinian dies of wounds

log.t: WAFA said an Israeli airstrike on Al-Shati camp killed three people on 5 Nov; Gaza's health ministry counts 1,602 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire. [119, 120]
src: Three Palestinians killed in Israeli airstrike on Gaza City
Four people, including a child, killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza

log.t: Gaza's health ministry reported 1,610 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire on 7 Nov; the first winter storm flooded about 70,000 tents. Israeli forces demolished buildings in Bani Hayyan and shelled areas south of Tyre; President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the first mandate to form a government. [28, 29, 173, 174]
src: Rains flood 70,000 displaced families' tents in Gaza
Israeli army continues strikes in southern Lebanon despite framework deal
Israel's president taps opposition candidate Eisenkot to form a government

log.t: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi drone and a ballistic missile aimed at southern Saudi Arabia on 1 Nov; Houthi media reported airstrikes on Ras Isa port and a telecoms site near Saada, with seven wounded at Ras Isa and the Bajil oil facility. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman raised the Houthi attacks with Hegseth on 3 Nov. [133, 134, 135]
src: Houthis report airstrikes on Red Sea oil port, telecom facility in Yemen
Saudi forces launch airstrike on port of Ras Isa, Yemen

log.t: The Houthis say Saudi strikes killed 17 people over two days; the Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed a drone over Mecca. [128]
A Houthi ballistic missile hit the al-Jumaima training camp in al-Dhalea, killing eight, a military source said; government forces claim ground in eastern al-Jawf. [33]
src: Yemeni government forces claim control of strategic al-Jawf mountain range

log.t: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a drone strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on 5 Nov; no Saudi statement on damage was published. [121, 122]
src: Trump weighs resuming Iran war as CENTCOM prepares for possible strikes (live updates, 5 Nov)
Houthis claim drone attack on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport

log.t: At least 30 people were killed at the al-Hadara market in Taiz on 6 Nov; the Houthis blame Saudi airstrikes and government forces blame Houthi missiles. [16]
src: Yemeni government forces, Houthis trade blame for deadly strikes on Taiz market

log.t: The Houthi health ministry said a strike it attributes to Saudi Arabia killed 33 at al-Shariya near Sanaa on 7 Nov; Saudi air defences intercepted a missile over Riyadh on 7 Nov and one toward the Eastern Province early on 8 Nov. No attack on shipping was reported. [30, 31, 32]
src: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
Yemeni gov't forces report advances as Houthis say deadly strikes hit Sanaa
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted ballistic missile fired toward eastern region

log.t: The Fifth Plenum (26–29 Oct) confirmed the expulsion of 33 senior officials, including 16 military officers and former Central Military Commission members Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli. Since 13 Oct, navy task groups including the carrier Liaoning have moved through the straits north and south of Taiwan. [64]

Taiwan's air force holds its annual Sky Dragon drills 2–6 Nov, and Kinmen held live-fire drills on 3 Nov. Premier Cho Jung-tai said Taiwan is still seeking a formal invitation to the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov. [26, 27, 28]
src: Taiwan air force holds annual Sky Dragon drills
Taiwan seeking formal APEC invitation from China: Premier

log.t: Taiwan's defence ministry logged 49 Chinese military aircraft sorties, six warships and six government vessels in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 4 Nov. [28]
Taiwan's defence ministry counted 21 Chinese military aircraft sorties, 19 of them across the median line, and eight navy and eight official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 5 Nov. [31]
src: PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan, 5 Nov

log.t: Taiwan's defence ministry counted three Chinese military aircraft sorties, nine navy ships and eight official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 6 Nov. [26]
src: PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan (2026.11.06)

log.t: Taiwan's defence ministry counted 11 Chinese military aircraft sorties, nine across the median line, 10 navy ships and three official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 7 Nov; on 6 Nov Taipei said it will close its representative office in Papua New Guinea. [17, 18]
src: PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan, 7 Nov 2026
Taiwan to close representative office in Papua New Guinea

log.t: Taiwan's defence ministry counted four PLA aircraft sorties, six navy ships and two official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 8 Nov; three more F-16Vs were due at Taitung on 8 Nov. [40, 42]
src: PLA activities in the waters and airspace around Taiwan, 8 Nov 2026
Second flight of F-16V jets from US expected today

log.t: North Korea fired a tactical ballistic missile with a cluster-bomb warhead on 31 Oct and strategic cruise missiles with a cluster warhead on 2 Nov, according to KCNA, while the Freedom Flag exercise runs at Kunsan to 6 Nov. [24, 25]
src: North Korea tests missile with cluster-bomb warhead
North Korea test-fires strategic cruise missiles: KCNA

log.t: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff say North Korea fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the East Sea on 4 Nov, the fourth launch event in a week. [26]
src: North Korea fires 'several missiles' east into the sea

log.t: KCNA said North Korea tested a new-type anti-aircraft missile system and held a strategic cruise missile drill on 4 Nov; South Korea's JCS detected several missiles from Sondok flying under 300 km. [28]
src: N. Korea says it test-fired new air defense missile system

log.t: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Workers' Party secretary Kim Song-nam in Beijing on 5 Nov; on 6 Nov North Korea's foreign ministry rejected the FATF's decision to keep it on the blacklist. [24, 25]
src: Chinese foreign minister, senior North Korean official meet in Beijing
North Korea lashes out at anti-laundering body over blacklist decision

log.t: KCNA reported a plenary meeting of the Supreme People's Assembly Standing Committee on 7 Nov. [19]
src: Plenary Meeting of DPRK SPA Standing Committee Held

log.t: The Supreme People's Assembly Standing Committee plenary was held on 5 Nov and reported by KCNA on 6 Nov; it recalled a vice chairman and amended two laws. Kim Song-nam met Cai Qi in Beijing on 6 Nov. The US State Department called for joint action after the Binance hack, which the FBI attributes to North Korea. [175, 44, 176]
src: N. Korea removes assembly vice chairman, amends construction, precious metal laws
N. Korean envoy holds 3rd high-level meeting in China
U.S. calls for coordinated action against N. Korean cyber threats following Binance hack

log.t: Drone strikes on 1 Nov destroyed the Al-Dabbah and Abu Hamad substations, days after hits on Shendi and the 500 MW Um Dabakir plant. A rights group counts 15 substations hit since early October; output is down from about 4,400 MW pre-war to 1,100 MW. Khartoum blames the RSF; the UAE denies arming the RSF. [63]
src: Sudan's power grid nears collapse as drone strikes target electric stations

log.t: Drones hit the New Halfa and Aroma stations in Kassala state and Al-Ghazali near Merowe on 2 Nov; Anadolu counts at least 16 stations hit in a week. Sudan filed complaints against Ethiopia at the UN Security Council and the African Union over drones it says came from Ethiopian territory. [22, 23]
src: Drone attacks hit 3 power stations in Sudan, trigger widespread outages
Sudan files complaints against Ethiopia with UN over deadly drone spree

log.t: Sudan's government says 187 drones in 70 attacks came from Ethiopian territory from February to October, killing 176 soldiers and 484 civilians; Ethiopia denies it. [29]
src: Deadly RSF drone strikes reveal deep divisions between Sudan and Ethiopia

log.t: Drones hit two power stations in Kassala and a substation at Merowe on 3 Nov and killed at least 12 civilians in West and South Kordofan on 2–3 Nov; the UN Secretary-General condemned the escalating drone attacks. [32]
src: Drone attacks kill civilians and cripple Sudan’s power infrastructure; UN warns of growing humanitarian toll

log.t: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council on 5 Nov that drone strikes are “a new and concerning dimension” in Abyei, where strikes on 19 Oct killed at least 30. [27]
src: Abyei: Deadly drone strikes mark 'new and concerning' threat, UN peacekeeping chief warns

log.t: The army-allied Joint Force said it took four villages west and south of El Obeid on 5 Nov; RSF videos dispute it. UN agencies said on 6 Nov that 15.4 million Sudanese need shelter. [20, 21]
src: Rival forces dispute control of North Kordofan areas
Sudan's suffering is plain to see, UN agencies say

log.t: Sudan's army said it shot down an FH-95 drone over Ayyal Bakhit in West Kordofan on 7 Nov; the IPC projects 825,000 children under five with severe acute malnutrition in 2026. [47, 48]
src: Sudanese army says it shot down 'hostile' drone in West Kordofan
Sudan war and climate change see parents struggle to feed their children

log.t: Algerian military personnel escorting fuel trucks reached Agadez, Niger, on the weekend of 1–2 Nov. [129]
src: Niger: Algerian military personnel have arrived in Agadez

log.t: Niger's and Mali's leaders met in Niamey on 6 Nov and said they had reiterated their determination to eradicate terrorism in the confederation. [24]
src: Les présidents nigérien et malien promettent d'éradiquer le terrorisme dans l'espace AES

log.t: MONUSCO's head met Joseph Kabila, leader of a rebel coalition that includes M23, in Goma on 3 Nov; more than 100,000 people marched for peace in Uvira on 4 Nov. [30, 31]
src: UN peacekeeping head meets leaders of rebel coalition in eastern DRC
Plus de 100 000 personnes marchent à Uvira pour exiger la paix

log.t: The FARDC and Wazalendo fighters attacked M23 positions in Masisi from 3 Nov; local sources report at least four civilians killed. [34]
src: Au moins quatre civils tués dans des affrontements entre les FARDC et le M23 à Masisi

log.t: Radio Okapi reports the FARDC and Wazalendo retook Mahanga and Kilongo in Masisi from the FRN on the night of 4–5 Nov; MONUSCO head James Swan visited Beni on 5 Nov. [28, 29]
src: Combats à Masisi : les FARDC reprennent le contrôle des villages de Mahanga et Kilongo
James Swan à Beni : « La protection des civils reste notre priorité »

log.t: Fighting between the FARDC and the FRN intensified on the Kashebere–Kibati axis in North Kivu on 6 Nov; a civil-society official said 24 civilians were killed near Beni overnight into 6 Nov. [22, 23]
src: Les combats s'intensifient entre les FARDC et le FRN sur l'axe Kashebere–Kibati
RDC : au moins 24 civils tués lors d'une attaque attribuée aux rebelles dans l'est du pays

log.t: Authorities raised the toll of the 5–6 Nov ADF attack in Beni to 33; Actualite.cd reported FRN rebels in Kalonge and Bitale in Kalehe on 7 Nov. [45, 46]
src: Death toll from ADF attack in DR Congo rises to 33
Sud-Kivu : Kalonge et Bitale passent sous contrôle des rebelles du FRN

log.t: Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco on 2 Nov; the State Department set out a “three-phase plan for Venezuela: stabilization, economic recovery and political reconciliation, and democratic transition.” [130]
src: US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition

log.t: OFAC designated two individuals, six entities and two vessels on 5 Nov under a new determination covering Cuba's electronics, manufacturing, marine and technology sectors. [123]
src: Recent actions, 5 November 2026: Cuba designations and Cuba-related determination

log.t: China's commerce ministry on 7 Nov urged the US “to correct its wrongdoings as soon as possible” after the State Department sanctioned CEIEC and Beijing H&C Technologies over supplies to Cuba's armed forces. [177]
src: Beijing urges US to correct its 'wrongdoings' swiftly after Washington sanctions Chinese companies over Cuba

theatres.name: Arctic and High North
theatres.scope: Northern Fleet activity and the Bastion; NATO High North exercises and Arctic Sentry; Greenland and the US defence areas; Svalbard; the Northern Sea Route and Russian and Chinese Arctic shipping; seabed cables and energy infrastructure in the Barents and Norwegian Seas.

log.t: Norway-led Cold Response 26 ended after ten days with about 25,000 troops from 14 nations exercising in northern Norway, Sweden and Finland; it began on 9 Mar. [1]
src: NATO's Arctic moves pose 'direct threat' to Russia, Lavrov says (background on Cold Response 26)

log.t: The Northern Fleet began a large naval exercise in the Barents Sea off the Rybachy peninsula near the Norwegian border, with the stated aim of engaging enemy naval formations. [1]
src: Northern Fleet kicks off large Barents-Arctic naval exercise

log.t: Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov wrote that NATO's Arctic activity, including the Arctic Sentry vigilance activity launched in February under Joint Force Command Norfolk, is a 'direct threat' to Russia's security and promised an 'asymmetric' response; SHAPE replied that the alliance is defensive and poses no threat to anyone. [1, 2]
src: NATO's Arctic moves pose 'direct threat' to Russia, foreign minister Lavrov says
Lavrov calls NATO's Arctic operations 'direct threat'

log.t: The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an arrangement supplementing the 1951 Greenland defence agreement at the UN General Assembly: the US may expand Pituffik Space Base and establish defence areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, with free movement between defence areas; new infrastructure needs trilateral consultation and Danish sovereignty is reaffirmed. Greenland's parliament later approved it. [1, 2]
src: Trump signs Greenland security deal allowing US to expand military presence
What to know about the agreement signed by President Trump and the leaders of Denmark and Greenland

log.t: The Barents Observer reported NOTAMs and navigational warnings for restricted areas near Franz Josef Land, Rybachy and Novaya Zemlya with overlapping periods, without a Northern Fleet announcement of a named exercise; NATO's Maritime Command said its High North posture is defensive and proportionate and that it will keep exercising and maintaining presence. [1, 2]
src: NATO maintains intensive surveillance amid Russian Arctic training and weapons testing
NATO rebuffs Russia's claims Arctic mission is direct threat

log.t: Norway detained the sanctioned, falsely flagged Chinese heavy-lift ship Ya Qing Hai Yang in the Andfjord near Andøya after a Northern Sea Route voyage. Greenland's parliament ratified the US–Denmark–Greenland defence agreement on 3 Nov; the Folketing votes on 19 Nov. Norway is deploying NASAMS sensors at Kirkenes against stray drones, and the sanctioned tanker Padre loitered on the Norway–Russia sea border from 19 Oct. HMS Prince of Wales operated in the Norwegian Sea under JFC Norfolk for Arctic Sentry. [35, 36, 37, 38, 171, 172]
src: After crossing Arctic route from China, two heavy lift carriers get stuck near Norwegian air base
Norway detains sanctioned Chinese ship sailing under false flag, inspects second vessel
Greenland parliament ratifies security deal reached with Trump
NASAMS sensors to be deployed along Norway's border with Russia
30-year-old tanker linked with Iran drifting along Norway's Arctic coast
UK and allied show of strength in the North
